name: Pit-seeking pipe coating
subtitle: a coating whose healing grains drift to rust

effects.effect: particles in a liquid drift along a difference in dissolved salt

effect: particles in a liquid drift along a difference in dissolved salt
how: Corrosion quietly eats pipelines, bridges and the steel inside concrete, and it starts in pits too small to see. A rusting pit leaks dissolved metal salts, so the water around it gets saltier toward the pit; tiny capsules of rust-stopper held in a damp gel layer drift up that salt slope on their own, pile into the pit and seal it, leaving healthy steel alone.
obstacle: The drift only works through a wet layer and over fractions of a millimetre, so capsules must already sit close to where a pit opens.
why: Repair goes only where damage starts, on infrastructure everyone depends on.
real: Self-healing coatings release inhibitors from pH- or redox-triggered reservoirs at corrosion sites, but nothing found on capsules migrating to pits by diffusiophoresis.
